Microsoft engages in more firefighting over Windows 10 upgrade anger

I've been in the IT field in the mid-west for over 20 years. Only thanks to Microsoft's heavy-handed approach with Windows 10 have I had requests by senior citizens on Linux. I have had the privilege of helping people whom I never imagined learn a new way of computing without Microsoft. I'm not saying this is the year of Linux...but it is nice to notice that winds are starting to blow in from a different direction.

To be honest, I really think there has been some inaccuracy about the latest upgrade window. I have seen one such window personally (but on someone else's computer so I don't know the steps leading up to said window). Click the X on the window does exactly what I would expect even given past X behaviour because the window that you are closing isn't asking you about upgrading; it's telling you that you are scheduled for the upgrade.

Closing a reminder window with the X never has cancelled or even changed the thing you are being reminded about (unless the reminder was additionally seeking input). This is no different.

Now that I have, in the interest of accuracy, said that, I still think that MS & Windows need to die.

I'll also add - I have a standing offer to anyone who wants to take me up on it; I will give you all the help I know how to & have time for to get you running Linux. This includes after the installation while trying to "get used to" it or with problems you may encounter.

I've lost all respect and confidence in MS as far as OS provider. I do have the Family subscription to Office as my wife and daughter use/need it for work and school, and I don't mind the 1 TB cloud backup for things that would fill up my Google Drive and Dropbox a bit too quickly. But I refuse to upgrade to 10 on principle. The OS is completely and totally out of my control no matter what I ultimately do, and if it weren't for games and a handful of Windows specific programs, I'd dump 8.1 in a heartbeat and load Ubuntu MATE. If MS had any sense, they would continue to provide the OS for free with no strings attached, no Telemetry, no bullshit and maybe they'd get some marketshare for their store. As it is, they're probably having to pay AAA devs to develop for the platform just to make it seem like it's a viable alternative to the App Store and Google Play. But even then, their retarded 'Modern' interface requires the devs to produce software that will run on the lowest common denominator (XBone and Windows Phone) and lacks features that are present in the same games/software offered by other companies. Their heads are so far up their asses because all they see us as are walking, talking wallets and audiences for billboard ads. They're seeing short term dollar signs trying to catch up with a business model that's already saturated with crap when they should be looking to start from a clean slate. Kill Windows, maybe not entirely, but start fresh with some backwards compatibility in terms of emulation/virtualization and begin to move onto something new rather than re-hashing old ideas. MS might own the desktop and PC games market, but that's not where things are heading. PC's won't entirely go away, but if they want true convergence, start working on a phone (and I think they may already have) that doubles as a PC when docked or connected to a keyboard, mouse and monitor. Canonical might beat them to the punch on that. We all probably have smartphones of one brand/OS or another that are quite capable given the hardware inside of also being a general purpose computer. Apple won't go down that road as they want you to buy as many of their devices as possible (iPhone, iMac, MacBook, iPad, etc.) and Google does a weak job with Chromebooks and Android. Give me a phone that can act as a PC when I need it to, keep backups of my files in the cloud with the option of also storing them on removable drives/media and I would be happy as a fucking clam.
